title: Handover from the Java loop test
content:
# Handover: results of the "scan → design doc → implement → verify" loop test on a Java project

Date: 2026-09-17. For the noesis SDLC planning session. Test project: `/Users/szjanikowski/Documents/git/itlibrium/discounts-java` (Gradle, Java 25, Lombok, vavr). Plugin: SDLC branch `szymon/noe-5-java-scanner` (PR #11), loaded with `--plugin-dir`. Everything below is recorded in the test repo; nothing in SDLC was changed.

## TL;DR

- The loop works end to end. Design doc via the skill in ~5 min with zero questions, implementation by a vanilla subagent, `compare_implementation_to_design` returned `Ok` with **zero problems on the first run** for both Sonnet and Opus, doc sealed.
- The structural gate is **blind to correctness**: Sonnet's and Opus's implementations produced **byte-identical after-scans**, yet a Fable code review found 10 findings in each, including a latent NPE (Sonnet only) and a hang path in the HTTP adapter (both).
- Thesis "automatic validation lets me use weaker models" holds only for naming/structure conformance. Opus removed the "own goal" class of defects on its own; neither model fixed pre-existing defects on the seam with old code, and neither questioned the adapter design the doc prescribed. Both need a review pass or a Java implementation skill with a seam check and an adapter checklist (NOE-8).
- Six prompt hints were required that should become part of a `plan-from-scan`/Java implementer skill (list in §5).

## 1. Where things are

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Baseline commit (stereotypes on all 15 domain types, `noesis-config.json`, design doc JSON, spec, before-scan) | branch `noesis-annotations`, commit `c56e4d6` |
| Sonnet implementation + its notes | branch `impl-sonnet`, commit `70b8795` (on top of `c56e4d6`) |
| Opus implementation + comparison notes | branch `impl-opus`, commit `626c891` (on top of `c56e4d6`) |
| Design doc | `noesis/design-docs/weather-based-discount-30e3293e.json`, id `01a0aecd-eac4-7000-bb41-9db530e3293e`, **sealed (implemented)** |
| Companion spec | `noesis-work/spec.md` |
| Scans | `noesis-work/before-scan.json` (baseline), `noesis-work/after-scan-1.json` (impl-sonnet), `noesis-work/after-scan-opus.json` (impl-opus) |
| Detailed notes | `noesis-work/notes.md` (impl-sonnet: steps 1–5 + Sonnet review), `noesis-work/notes-opus.md` (impl-opus: Opus run + Sonnet-vs-Opus table) |
| Skill scratch files | `~/.noesis-plugin-data/projects/a6a102ffbfc2/tmp/noesis:create-design-doc/01a0aecd-eac4-7000-bb41-9db530e3293e/` |
| Requirements used | "Weather-Based Discount": 10 % off when Open-Meteo reports precipitation > 0 for Warsaw; must be easy to add temperature/wind/cloud/humidity/UV variants; API failures must not break order processing; unit + integration tests |

Note: the annotations artifact is `vision.noesis:noesis-annotations:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` from `mavenLocal()`; a fresh clone does not build without `mvn install` in `noesis/scanners/java`.

## 2. Timings

| Step | Wall time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 scan + summary | ~3 min | baseline redone once (Offer/Product stereotype fix) before any doc existed |
| 2 spec | ~5 min chat | one proposal, accepted as is |
| 3 `create-design-doc` skill | 11:58 → 12:03 (~5 min) | green-field short-circuit (empty graph), no `AskUserQuestion` fired |
| 3b manual JSON edit + re-save | ~1 min | no skill re-run needed |
| 4 implement, Sonnet | 12:20 → 12:28 (~8 min, ~20 turns) | 14 tests |
| 4 implement, Opus | 13:48 → 13:52 (~4 min, ~9 turns) | 19 tests |
| 5 scan + compare + seal | ~3 min | Ok on first run, both models |
| code review `/code-review high` (Fable) | ~3 min each | ~75–80 k tokens per review |

## 3. What the scanner / comparator did (NOE-5)

Baseline model: BC `discounts`, modules `calculation` (14 blocks), `offers` (2), `users` (3). Package layout is flat, so the dotted-module convention was exercised only by the new `weather.openmeteo`; it held: declaring `weather` as an added module and `weather.openmeteo` as another added module matched scanned `fullPath`s with no intermediate-prefix issue.

Scanner observations:
- Several types per file work (Discount.java → 4 blocks). Package-private classes and interfaces are seen.
- `default` interface methods count as behaviours. **Overloads collapse to one name** (`ProductDiscount.apply` ×2 → one entry).
- Lombok-generated getters/constructors are invisible (correct, source-only).
- `@Adapter` → type `Adapter`, `@Port` → type `Port`; the design doc uses `external_integration` for both. Types are not compared, so no effect on compare, but the vocabulary differs between scanner and schema.
- Empty annotated class (`Product`) is a block; unannotated `App.java` is skipped.
- Diff before → after was exactly the 12 declared items (2 modules, 5 blocks, 5 behaviours). **Noise: 0. Real mismatches: 0.**

Comparator (`comparison.ts`): `modified` entries only require presence after implementation and never yield "unexpected"; a `modified` block with no scanner-visible change (field added, call added) is safe. The gate is by name/position only, as documented.

## 4. What the design-doc tooling did (NOE-6)

- **Empty graph → BC in code must be bucketed `modified`**, per schema §3. Consequence: `read_design_doc` rendered `Bounded Contexts: (none)` because it renders `added` only. The implementer had to be handed the JSON file path, not the rendering. Known gap, now confirmed as blocking for the implement step, not just lossy for iteration.
- **`save_design_doc` validation is effectively empty for references.** `implements: ["Discount"]`, `implements: ["PotentialDiscount"]`, input/output/usedBuildingBlocks pointing at `Conditions`, `DiscountedOffer`, `DiscountAmount` — all exist only in code, not in the graph — saved with 0 errors, 0 warnings. A typo would have passed too and surfaced only at compare. Suggest: validate references against the scan (or a scan-derived model) when the graph is empty.
- **Save normalises the file**: after save the JSON gained 127 `*_locked: false` flags (name, description, type, actor, given/when/then). Harmless, but hand edits must expect the file to be rewritten.
- **Manual iteration path works**: edit JSON → `save_design_doc` with the same canonical path → Ok. Used to add change notes to `modified` blocks. Confirms the skill is only needed when requirements change.
- **Feedback (user):** for `modified` building blocks the schema rule "omit description when unchanged" leaves the reader with no prose about what changed (`Conditions`, `DiscountPolicyFactory`, `DiscountsConfigProvider` had empty descriptions). Suggest the skill emit a short change note in `description` on every `modified` item, at least when the graph has no description for it yet.
- **UI idea (user):** a toggle in the design-doc view that renders the diff *against* the existing model (full tree, added/modified/removed highlighted). The graph has the model after a UI scan and the doc has the delta, so it should be an overlay. The same overlay would fix `read_design_doc` for the agent.
- Skill quality: the six analysis files were sensible; no contradictions; no question needed. Behaviour names had to be Java identifiers (`getCurrent`, `isApplicableFor`), overriding the schema's PascalCase convention — done via the invocation prompt.

## 5. Prompt hints that were necessary (candidates for skills)

For `create-design-doc` (→ `plan-from-scan`):
1. Baseline is the scanner JSON, not the graph (skill §1.0a/§1.3/§1.5 read the graph, which was empty).
2. Behaviour names = code identifiers, not PascalCase.
3. Modules as dotted path relative to BC.
4. No actors (Java scanner returns null).
5. Existing BC/modules/blocks go to `modified`, never `added`.

For the implementer (→ NOE-8 Java skill), given verbatim to both subagents:
1. Read the design-doc **JSON file** (not `read_design_doc` output); ignore `*_locked`.
2. Read 6–8 named existing classes first; follow Lombok/vavr/package-private conventions.
3. Package = group id + dotted module path.
4. Class and method names exactly as in the doc; **no extra non-private methods, no extra top-level types** (otherwise "unexpected change" noise). Parse JSON as a tree to avoid a DTO type.
5. Stereotype mapping incl. `@Port` / `@Adapter(Direction.SECONDARY)` as used by the existing adapter; where to inspect the annotation jar.
6. Build with Gradle (handover said `mvn`); tests must not touch the network (JDK `HttpServer` stub).

With these hints both models produced scanner-clean code on the first attempt. Without hint 4 the risk of noise is high (a DTO class or a helper method would be an unexpected block/behaviour).

## 6. Code quality: Sonnet vs Opus (same prompt, same doc)

| | Sonnet | Opus |
|---|---|---|
| time / turns / tests | ~8 min / ~20 / 14 | ~4 min / ~9 / 19 |
| scanner + comparator | Ok, identical after-scan | Ok, identical after-scan |
| defects introduced by the model itself | `Conditions.weather` plain `@Builder` field → null when omitted (latent NPE); `InterruptedException` swallowed; 5 s sleep in timeout test; trailing-slash URL breaks silently; redundant double catch | data race on a `StringBuilder` in one test; handler thread sleeping 6 s past `server.stop` |
| pre-existing seam defects left in place | `FixedDiscount` still records `DiscountAmount(null)` while new `PercentageDiscount` records `DiscountAmount(this)` → NPE in `ExclusiveOfferLevelDiscount` for VIP + rain; `ExclusiveOfferLevelDiscount.isInstance` is inverted (always false) — the doc says exclusivity relies on this class | same two |
| adapter-design defects shared by both | `HttpRequest.timeout` bounds headers only → stalled body hangs `calculate` forever; synchronous HTTPS on every calculation; catch-all with no logging; `HttpClient` per instance, never closed; `percentage` unvalidated | same |

Reading: Opus self-corrected the "own goals" (null default, interrupt flag, URL, test duration, covariant return, javadoc) without being told. Neither model looked across the seam into pre-existing code it had been told to read and that the doc named as load-bearing, and neither challenged the prescribed adapter shape. Reviews are non-deterministic: the Opus review dug deeper and found the shared adapter defects that the Sonnet review missed; I verified they apply to Sonnet's tree too.

Implications for NOE-8 (Java implementer skill):
- Add a mandatory **seam check**: for every `modified` block, diff conventions between new and existing code paths (constructors, null markers, helper usage) and report/align.
- Add an **adapter checklist**: timeout covering body read (`sendAsync().get(timeout)` or `orTimeout`), WARN log on failure, injectable `HttpClient` or `AutoCloseable`, input validation on value objects, no per-call I/O when no registered policy needs it.
- Keep hint 4 (no extra public surface) — it is what made the comparator clean.
- Expect Sonnet + skill ≈ acceptable; Opus without skill ≈ acceptable minus seam; neither is safe without a review pass. The structural gate cannot replace review; it removes only the naming/placement class of errors.

## 7. Known-gap table, updated

| Gap | Observed | Status |
|---|---|---|
| No `@Actor`, scanner returns null | not exercised (no actors declared) | open, NOE-8 |
| `create-design-doc` reads the graph, not the scan, as baseline | forced by prompt; worked | open, NOE-6; with empty graph the doc is still correct, but references are unvalidated |
| `read_design_doc` renders `added` only | **blocking** for implementer when BC is `modified` | open, NOE-6; overlay view idea above |
| `save_design_doc` barely validates | confirmed: dangling refs accepted silently | open, NOE-6 |
| types/rules/scenarios not compared | confirmed: `Port`/`Adapter` vs `external_integration` not flagged; correctness defects invisible | open, NOE-13 / scanner |
| simple-name annotation matching | not exercised (no JPA/Spring) | open, NOE-12 |
| overloads collapse to one behaviour | new observation | scanner, minor |
| `save_design_doc` rewrites file with `*_locked` flags | new observation | cosmetic |
| `modified` blocks lose their description in the doc | new observation (user feedback) | NOE-6 |

## 8. Side notes

- The Eclipse JDT language server used by the IDE created `.project`, `.settings/`, `app/.classpath`, `app/.factorypath`, `app/bin/` and reports false Lombok/Jackson errors; not produced by subagents; not committed; `.gitignore` should cover them.
- Subagent self-reports overstate test counts (Sonnet claimed 20, XML says 14). Count from `app/build/test-results` rather than trusting the report.
- `/code-review high` on ~300 changed lines cost ~75–80 k tokens and ~3 min per run; findings quality was good, with 2 of 10 environment-only items each time.
